clue.text: Dance with former copper and seem clumsy

indicators.note: something done clumsily is botched and out of order, so the word before is jumbled

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone dancing alongside a retired policeman looks awkward on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: An excuse-me is a ballroom dance in which a partner may be claimed by someone cutting in.
explanation.definitionFit: The excuse-me is a named social dance where people politely interrupt couples to change partners.

clue.text: Soldier who carries the Colours in? Gen's misleading

indicators.note: something misleading leads astray, so these letters wander from their order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: A question about the flag-bearer, answered by blaming a general for giving bad directions.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark breaks the clue in two; 'in' belongs to the fodder, not the definition. Colours are a regiment's flags.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign was historically the junior officer who bore the regimental flag into battle.

clue.text: Fried potato - a lot cooked, served with a sausage

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: a chip is a fried strip of potato

explanation.surface: A plate of chips, plenty of them, served alongside a banger.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a menu; 'cooked' seems to describe the meal but signals rearranging. A banger is a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin type of sausage, often served at breakfast.

clue.text: Hires Mark, disciple

blocks.note: a son can mean a follower or spiritual disciple

explanation.surface: A list: someone hires Mark, the gospel writer and disciple.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like the evangelist's name, but it is just a sign or symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign someone on is to take them on as an employee, which is a phrasal synonym for hiring.

clue.text: Unseen establishment figures, good inside foreign ministry? (Unseen mostly)

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter of the bracketed word goes
foreign suggests something strange and altered, so the letters are rearranged
inside tells us one piece sits within the rearranged letters

blocks.note: the bracketed word less its last letter
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Faceless officials, decent at heart, working in an overseas government department.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed instruction adds the shortened word to the fodder. The answer is an idiom for anonymous bureaucrats who wield power quietly behind the scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes anonymous, powerful officials whose influence operates behind the scenes, i.e. hidden people of the establishment.

clue.text: Material's marvellous, very amusing once abridged

indicators.note: abridging cuts something short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: fab is slang for fabulous, marvellous
'that's rich' means very amusing, ironic or laughable

explanation.surface: A review of some cloth: it is marvellous, and was once very funny before being cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric is cloth or textile, a direct synonym for material used to make clothes.

clue.text: Offensive, a sailor reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as told by word of mouth, so the sound of the phrase is what counts

blocks.note: a salt is an old sailor

explanation.surface: Someone finds a seaman objectionable, as the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Offensive looks like an adjective, but here it is a noun: a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An offensive is a military attack, so the noun is a synonym for an assault.

clue.text: Possessed girl, a daughter of King Lear

blocks.note: first meaning: the demon-possessed child in the film The Exorcist
second meaning: one of the two scheming elder daughters in Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.walkthrough: Both meanings are the same girl's name, from a horror film and from Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the child in The Exorcist and to Lear's middle daughter in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Spurn girl initially, girl with a refined accent?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: to cut someone is to snub or spurn them

explanation.surface: Rebuffing a posh-sounding girl.
explanation.walkthrough: A cut-glass accent is a very precise upper-class English one, clear and sharp like crystal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut-glass describes speech that is crisp and upper-class, so it fits a person speaking with a refined, posh accent.

clue.text: Military manoeuvre - could it be the making of prince?

blocks.clueFragment: could it be the making of prince?
blocks.note: surface reading: a campaign that might make a young royal's name

blocks.clueFragment: could it be the making of prince?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a movement of the letters of 'prince' makes the name of a gripping tool

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a battlefield tactic could make a young royal into a hero.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half hints that shifting the letters of 'prince' produces the first word of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pincer movement is a tactic in which forces attack an enemy from two flanks at once, closing like jaws.

clue.text: Very little fly found in tin

indicators.note: found in places one piece within the other

blocks.note: a midge is a small fly
Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: A tiny insect has turned up inside a can.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgen is a tiny amount, so it is a noun synonym for a very small quantity.

clue.text: Understanding of current things in variety

indicators.note: variety implies different arrangements, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Grasping what is happening now across a range of matters.
explanation.walkthrough: Current looks like 'present-day', but it is the physics symbol for electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep grasp or perception of something, a synonym for understanding.

clue.text: Show deficit after end of trading

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word that follows
after says the first piece comes behind the second when written down

explanation.surface: A business reports a shortfall at the close of the trading day.
explanation.walkthrough: Show looks like a command but is a noun: a surface appearance or sheen.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloss is a superficial attractive appearance, so it means outward show hiding something less pleasant.

clue.text: Active at night? No? Go in around beginning of Lent

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the abbreviation that follows
beginning of picks out the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: a go or turn in a game

explanation.surface: A question and refusal about staying out late, with a nod to giving things up for Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: Go is a noun here, a turn; circa is abbreviated ca.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal animals are awake and active during the hours of darkness, sleeping by day.

clue.text: Film makers run into trouble blocking those advising caution?

indicators.note: into puts the abbreviation inside the word for trouble
blocking means standing in the middle of something, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone runs into difficulties by obstructing the people trying to warn them.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions: the run goes into the trouble, and that whole word then splits the cautioners before their final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Warner Brothers is the Hollywood studio, a company that produces films.

clue.text: Attention given to female in pub, incessant talker

indicators.note: in places the word for a woman within the drinking place

blocks.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A woman in a pub gets noticed by someone who will not stop chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: An earbasher is Australian and British slang for someone who talks on and on, bashing your ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who bashes your ear talks at you relentlessly, so the slang word means a nonstop chatterer.

clue.text: Heather following barge, glowering

indicators.note: following puts the first piece behind the second when written

blocks.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed barge

explanation.surface: Heather walks behind a narrowboat with a frown on her face.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Scowling means frowning angrily, a participle synonym for glowering.

clue.text: Crony, architect, organised benefit show

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pal of the architect has put together a fundraising performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A charity concert is a musical performance staged to raise money for a cause, which is a benefit.

clue.text: Be left at home with that girl, Italian

blocks.note: It is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck at home with an Italian girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Be left is meant in the sense of being bequeathed something in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to receive property in a will, i.e. to be left it by someone who has died.

clue.text: Legend, suitable, I displayed in study

indicators.note: displayed in places the pieces inside the word for study

blocks.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A notice says a suitable item was on show in someone's study.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend means the text under a picture or map, not a famous person.
explanation.definitionFit: A caption is the explanatory text accompanying an illustration, which is also called a legend.

clue.text: Somebody deserving

blocks.note: first meaning: an important or notable person

explanation.walkthrough: Somebody here is a noun meaning a person of importance, as in 'a local worthy'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word names a notable dignitary; as an adjective it means meriting respect or reward.

clue.text: We do, after a struggle, accommodate writer

indicators.note: a struggle leaves things thrown about, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: After a fight, we agree to put up an author.
explanation.walkthrough: P. G. Wodehouse wrote the Jeeves and Wooster stories.
explanation.definitionFit: P. G. Wodehouse was the English comic novelist, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Give way in Grande ferry

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Yielding to other boats on a ferry on the Rio Grande.
explanation.definitionFit: To defer is to yield or submit to another's wishes, which is a synonym for giving way.

clue.text: Trouble after advertising Madrid gallery

indicators.note: after places the first piece behind the second when written

explanation.surface: Difficulties follow a promotional campaign for a Spanish museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prado is Spain's national art museum, located in the capital Madrid.

clue.text: Stylish defence saving one heading towards trouble

indicators.note: saving means keeping safe within, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: a fort is a defensive building
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A smart defensive play in a match rescues a player who is about to get into a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in for it is an idiom for being about to face punishment, so likely to get into trouble.

clue.text: English PM suppressing ambassador's nickname

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down and keeping in, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
William Pitt, father and son, were British prime ministers
His Excellency is an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: A British prime minister silences a diplomat's pet name.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', a common way to supply a pronoun-like abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive byname added to someone's name, so it can serve as a nickname.

clue.text: Go round Ayr and get lost

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so the letters wander out of order

blocks.note: Ayr is a town on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: Drive round a Scottish town and lose your way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get lost' looks like a rude dismissal, but 'get' is fodder and 'lost' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to revolve or spin about a centre, a verb synonym for going round.

clue.text: Ratings cooked unknown fish

indicators.note: cooking transforms things, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: Sailors prepared some mysterious seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratings are ordinary sailors in the surface, but here just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat cartilaginous sea creature, an example of a fish.
